fatal_errors: The proposed post-quench hold cannot improve amorphous retention during solidification, because solidification and any associated crystallization have already occurred before the hold.
The intervention misses the central compositional change to Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 and the comparison between arc cooling and 40 m/s melt spinning.
The cited evidence discusses cooling-rate and phosphorus effects but provides no support for sub-Tg annealing, free-volume reduction, or delayed devitrification.
A glass transition was not detected in the target system, so specifying a sub-Tg treatment is not experimentally grounded.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses thermal stability and supplies a reasonably falsifiable quenched-versus-held comparison, but it does not reconstruct the reported intervention or mechanism. The target achieved eutectic-dominated solidification and full ribbon amorphization by changing Fe/Co/Mn/P composition and rapidly melt spinning approximately 20 micrometer ribbon at 40 m/s; slower arc cooling still produced segregated solid solution and phosphides. By contrast, the proposed post-quench relaxation treatment cannot increase the glass fraction established during solidification and may instead promote incipient crystallization. Its conditions also omit the demonstrated 20 K/min reheating boundary and use an undefined sub-Tg window despite the absence of an observed Tg. The experiment could test aging effects on an already formed glass, but it does not test the target composition-processing hypothesis, and the cited passages do not validate the proposed mechanism.
